=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- CLAUDE.md:2250-2257 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: §28.C still instructs issue-mode failure escalations to send a PushNotification and wait for a human `/reclarify`, contradicting the escalation judge hand-off and §28.G.
  WHY: A session following §28.C can notify and wait instead of handing the escalation to the judge, contrary to §28.G’s rule that only `close` notifies.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md:36-45 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The judge is not instructed to include the PR number in `--why` when recording an `intervention-cap` choice, although the cap-counting rule requires `why=` to name the same PR.
  WHY: The resumed stage may fail to associate the budget grant with the blocked PR, count no extra round, and re-escalate after the ledger has made the same choice unavailable.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md:1,17 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The root command says the same choice cannot be picked twice for a failure, incorrectly implying that `close` cannot be repeated.
  WHY: This contradicts `escalation_ledger.py` and the test asserting that `close` can repeat, so a judge following the command may rule out a valid choice.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:294 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The root command says the same escalation choice cannot be used twice for a failure, incorrectly implying that `close` cannot be repeated.
  WHY: This contradicts the ledger behavior and the documented invariant that `close` stays available.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md:25 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The root command omits `pr` from its evidence keys, while the root `escalation_ledger.py` lacks the PR-scoped fingerprint logic and required-PR guard for `intervention-cap` and `fix-check-defective`.
  WHY: Failures on different PRs can share a fingerprint, causing their escalation choices to be treated as the same failure.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md:52-53 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Both step 8 branches in the root command end the turn instead of continuing to step 9.
  WHY: The session skips step 9’s permission-prompt report.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:321 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The intervention-cap counting rule scopes budget grants using a free-text `why=` PR reference, although the judge is not instructed to include the PR number and the fingerprint already scopes the failure to a PR.
  WHY: Without that reference, the resumed stage may count zero extra rounds and immediately re-escalate; the PR-scoped fingerprint already distinguishes the PRs.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: “Escalation: ES-<n> <budget | descope> (stop <stop id>) — <the narrower fix | the de-scoped part>” | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The resume line template omits the PR number, although the next stage must supply `pr` evidence to fingerprint `intervention-cap` or `fix-check-defective`.
  WHY: A stage relying on the resume block may not recover the PR needed by `escalation_ledger.py fingerprint`.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A failure is its stop id plus a fingerprint: the SHA-1 (first 12 hex characters) of the normalised failing check names, finding ids, follow-up issue numbers, validation class and status, and the PR the stop is about (required for intervention-cap and fix-check-defective, so two PRs that fail the same way never share a fingerprint)"
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The on-disk .claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py (318 lines) has none of these symbols. The twin at workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py (343 lines) has all of them. The .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md root copy step 2 evidence keys list omits pr. The twin includes it. These are documented as awaiting the [claude-twin-sync] copy.
- requirement: "Step 8 branches continue to step 9 for the permission-prompt report"
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md step 8 lines 52-53
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: On-disk .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md step 8 budget/descope branch at line 52 says "Report and end the turn" (twin says "Continue with step 9") and close branch at line 53 says "End the turn" (twin says "Continue with step 9"). The twin has the correct text after commit 602b18f.
- requirement: Issue-mode failure escalations are handed to the escalation judge without a stop notification or a human `/reclarify` wait.
  expected_change_site: CLAUDE.md §28.C, “Failure escalations”
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The existing §28.C text still says "delivered on the source issue: one comment naming the blocker, the options, and the recommended one, the `ai:claude-blocked` label, and one `PushNotification`" and "A human answers there and comments /reclarify to resume."; CLAUDE.md:2251-2253 still instructs issue-mode stops to send one `PushNotification` and says a human answers with `/reclarify`. That conflicts with the new §28.G notification rule at CLAUDE.md:2427-2429, which says escalation stops send no notification and only `close` notifies.
- requirement: “It never picks the same choice twice for the same failure fingerprint.”
  expected_change_site: `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py::allowed_choices()` and `record_line()`, with coverage in `tests/test_escalation_ledger.py`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `allowed_choices()` always includes `close`, even when that choice is already recorded for the stop and fingerprint, and `record_line()` consequently permits recording it again. `tests/test_escalation_ledger.py::test_record_refuses_a_used_choice` explicitly asserts that a second `close` succeeds.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- CLAUDE.md: lines 2250-2256 (§28.C "Failure escalations" bullet) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure-escalation paragraph still says issue-mode stops send "one PushNotification" with "one comment naming the blocker, the options, and the recommended one, the ai:claude-blocked label, and one PushNotification" and "A human answers there and comments /reclarify to resume." The appended sentence "These stops are not auto-decided, but they no longer wait for a human: the escalation judge answers them" cannot suppress the earlier instruction — a session reading §28.C encounters both directives and may follow the older PushNotification and human-wait instruction alongside the new judge hand-off.
  WHY: An interactive Claude session running an issue-mode escalation stop follows §28.C and sends a PushNotification the §28.G contract forbids, then may present the obsolete /reclarify resume path. The implement-plan-claude.md Issue Mode bullet and §28.G both say only close notifies; CLAUDE.md §28.C says all escalation stops notify via PushNotification. The two sections conflict.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md: line 1 ("never pick a choice already used for the same failure") and line 17 ("The same failure never gets the same choice twice") | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The on-disk .claude/ root copy still uses the older "never the same choice twice" wording that incorrectly implies close cannot be repeated. The twin (workflow-templates/.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md) correctly says "never pick budget or descope twice for the same failure (close stays available)" after commit 602b18f. The root copy is what a session reads at runtime; the twin is for sync only.
  WHY: An escalation judge reading the .claude/ root copy will believe close cannot be repeated, contradicting escalation_ledger.py's allowed_choices() which always includes close and test_record_refuses_a_used_choice which explicitly asserts close can repeat. The test contract and the runtime behavior disagree with the command text.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 294 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The on-disk .claude/ root copy says "never the same one twice for the same failure (.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py)" — implying close also cannot repeat. The twin (workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:294) correctly says "never budget or descope twice for the same failure (.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py; the fingerprint of a PR-scoped stop includes the PR number)". The word-level edit did not sync into the root copy.
  WHY: A stage reading this line incorrectly believes close is consumed once per failure, which contradicts the ledger's allowed_choices() and the documented invariant that close stays available.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md: line 25 (root copy, step 2 evidence keys: "keys: checks, findings, issues, validation_class, validation_status; leave out what the stop does not have") | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The on-disk .claude/ root copy step 2 lists the evidence keys without pr, and step 8 branches end the turn at line 52 ("Report and end the turn.") and line 53 ("End the turn.") rather than continuing to step 9. The twin (75 lines) includes pr in the evidence key list and both step 8 branches say "Continue with step 9." The escalation_ledger.py root copy (318 lines) also lacks PR_SCOPED_STOP_IDS, EVIDENCE_PR_KEY, _normalise_pr, and the pr-required guard in fingerprint() — the twin (343 lines) has all of these.
  WHY: When a session hits intervention-cap or fix-check-defective, running the root copy of escalation_ledger.py does not require pr in the evidence and does not include it in the fingerprint, so two PRs that fail the same way share a fingerprint and each other's choices. Running the root copy of escalation-judge.md with step 8 ending the turn at "Report and end the turn." skips step 9's permission-prompt report.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md: step 5 Record, lines 41-45; cross-ref implement-plan-claude.md line 321 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The judge records --why as free-text with no instruction to include the PR number for intervention-cap stops. The cap-counting rule in implement-plan-claude.md line 321 says "for intervention-cap, only entries whose why= names the same PR" — but nothing in the judge command requires or suggests the PR number go into why=. The pr evidence key was added to the fingerprint in commit 602b18f, which prevents cross-PR fingerprint collisions, but the why=-based cap counting is a separate mechanism that the judge is not told about.
  WHY: The judge writes why=retry the CI fix for intervention-cap on PR #12. The resumed stage reads the ES entry and cannot match PR #12 in the free-text why=. The extra round does not count, the stage immediately re-escalates, and the same fingerprint then shows budget as already used (allowed returns descope, close). The budget grant was recorded but had no effect.
